description: The asset types a Shared Workspace can hold, derived from AUB's actual asset model rather than transcribed from a product document: `maps`, `texture_sources`, `entity_catalogues`, `game_profiles` and the user prefab packages are collections that already exist. Two flags per type carry the V1 restrictions that the rest of the contract leans on. `mutable` says whether the type has an in-place edit path and therefore an Offline edit lease at all; `realtime_eligible` says whether it can escalate into an AUC session. Only the map is either, and that is the V1 decision, not an oversight: there is no whole-workspace session and no live collaborative editing of a texture binary.

asset_types.summary: An APMap document. The only type with an Offline edit lease and the only Real-time primary object.

A WAD or a texture package. It has durable revisions — a replacement upload bumps one — but no in-place edit path, so it takes no lease. A future type that gains one gets its own exclusive Offline lock; it does not get the map's escalation path with it.
Entity definitions a map is authored against.
A game profile. Platform-owned default profiles are referenced by a map without becoming workspace assets; only a user-owned profile is attachable.

revision_note: Every attachable asset carries a revision whether or not it is `mutable`. Mutability decides whether there is a lease; the revision decides whether a write is accepted, and a replacement upload of an immutable type is a write like any other.
